hook_line: COMMENT WINDOW CLOSES ON PLAN TO END DEFERENCE FOR H-1B EXTENSIONS

hook_stat.sub: Extension petitions a year that DHS estimates would lose deference

stats.label: H-1B continuing-employment approvals for workers born in India
Additional requests for evidence expected a year
H-1B extension filers that were small entities

diaspora_bullets: H-1B petitions make up more than 75% of all Form I-129 filings, according to DHS
A timely filed H-1B extension lets the worker keep working for up to 240 days after the I-94 expires
news_summary: The public comment period on the proposal to end deference for work-visa extensions closed on November 13, 2026, and the deference regulation stays in force unless DHS publishes a final rule.
payoff: There is nothing to file now; the next step is DHS publishing a final rule, and no date for one has been set.
